title: A key that is too small
prompt: A message encrypted with RSA, with a public key small enough to break. Each number is one letter (A=1 … Z=26). The flag is flag{word} in lower case.
hint.1: RSA is only safe when n is too big to factor. Factor n into two primes.
hint.2: With p and q you can compute the private exponent d, the inverse of e modulo (p-1)(q-1). The Cipher Quest RSA helper does it.
hint.3: n = 101 × 103. Decrypt each number as number^d mod n and turn it back into a letter.
walkthrough: Factor n, compute d, decrypt each number and read the letters. The word is lower-cased inside flag{...}.
